'''Earl Jay Taft''' (1931 – August 9, 2021){{r|born}} was an American mathematician specializing in [[abstract algebra]]. He is the namesake of the [[Taft Hopf algebra]]{{r|dkl}} which he introduced in a 1971 publication,{{r|pnas}} and he was the founding editor of the journal ''[[Communications in Algebra]]''.{{r|edit}} He was Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at [[Rutgers University]].{{r|dem}}

==Education and career==
Taft graduated from [[Amherst College]] in 1952.{{r|ias}} He completed his doctorate at [[Yale University]] in 1956. His dissertation, ''Invariant Wedderburn Factors'', was supervised by [[Nathan Jacobson]].{{r|mg}} After working as [[Joseph Ritt|Ritt]] Instructor of mathematics at [[Columbia University]] from 1956 to 1959,{{r|ias}} he moved to [[Rutgers University]], where he remained for many years.{{r|acs}} He was also a regular visitor to the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].{{r|ias}}

==Personal life==
Taft's wife, [[Hessy Levinsons Taft]], had been publicized as "the most beautiful Aryan baby" in Nazi propaganda despite being Jewish. Her family escaped [[Nazi]] Germany for [[France]], Cuba, and later the US, and she met Taft as a graduate student in [[chemistry]] at [[Columbia University]], while he was an instructor there.{{r|acs}}

After Taft retired from Rutgers, he and his wife moved to New York City.{{r|acs}} Taft died in San Francisco at the age of 89.<ref name=obit>{{citation |title=Earl Taft obituary | newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=August 15, 2021 |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/nytimes/name/earl-taft-obituary?id=14493314}}</ref>
